state:
Goal `core-response-and-1-more`: `Core\Response::addCookie` has every feature proof — `about.md`,
three examples with `.nvsr` requests, the attack, the bench record in `docs/perf/members.ndjson`,
and two Rust `#[test]`s carrying `covers:` in `crates/nvs-stdlib/src/response.rs`.
`Core\Response` now carries its class card; `Core\Response\Stream` is still in
`CLASSES_STILL_OWING_A_CARD` in `crates/nvs-stdlib/src/registry.rs`, and `Core\Response\Stream::write`
owes it. Nothing is blocked.

`nvs run --request` prints the response body alone, never the status line or the headers. An
example for a member that writes only the head therefore shows its effect in a body line it writes
itself, and the Rust test pins the header line (`every_written_option_is_one_attribute_and_each_call_is_one_line`).

next.title: body members
next.note: one file set: `crates/nvs-stdlib/src/response.rs` (the body helpers and the `tests` module), `docs/examples/core/Response/`, `tests/hostile/core/Response/`, `benches/members/core/Response/`. Each example needs a `.nvsr` request beside it, as the `addCookie` ones have.

items.text: **`Core\Response::bytes`** — owes about, examples, hostile, perf, Rust `covers:` (`rule:security/response-body-is-one-typed-member`). The Rust half is a `// covers:` line on `each_body_member_sets_its_own_content_type` at `crates/nvs-stdlib/src/response.rs:1997`; the member is `crates/nvs-stdlib/src/response.rs:1674`.
**`Core\Response::html`** — the same owed set; member at `crates/nvs-stdlib/src/response.rs:1062`, and the same test takes its `covers:` line. `html` takes a `Core\Html\Markup`, never a `string`.

backlog: `setHeader`, `setStatus` and `redirect` write only the response head, which no `.out` can show; their examples print a body line, and their Rust tests pin the head (the `addCookie` pattern).
